excerpt: Rented mat exchange programs and purchased mats maintained by your janitorial crew are priced on completely different units, which makes them hard to compare. This guide converts both into per-mat, per-sq-ft, and hourly figures with minimum charges so you can see the real monthly cost.
quickAnswer: Mat exchange programs typically run $2.50-$5 per swap for a 3 x 5 ft mat, $4-$8 for a 4 x 6 ft, and $7-$14 for a 3 x 10 ft runner, plus a $10-$25 per-stop service charge, so weekly swaps cost about $11-$61 per mat per month. Purchased mats vacuumed by your crew add only 1-3 labor minutes per mat per visit, usually absorbed in a $0.07-$0.15 per sq ft base rate, with periodic hot-water extraction at $0.30-$0.60 per sq ft of mat or $35-$65 per hour.

blocks.text: Entrance matting is the cheapest floor protection you can buy: industry studies regularly cite that most soil in a commercial building arrives on shoes, and 15-20 feet of walk-off matting captures the majority of it. The question for an office manager is how to pay for that matting. A mat exchange program, run by uniform and linen route companies, bills per mat per swap and delivers a freshly laundered mat on a fixed cycle. A purchased mat program puts mats you own on the floor and relies on your janitorial vendor to vacuum them nightly and deep-clean them periodically. One is a recurring service invoice; the other is a capital purchase plus labor minutes buried in your cleaning rate.
National unit pricing for mat exchange programs

blocks.caption: Typical US rental mat exchange pricing (per mat, per swap)
headers: Per sq ft of mat per month, weekly

blocks.text: On top of the per-swap price, most route companies add a per-stop service or delivery charge of $10-$25, a fuel or environmental surcharge of 3%-8%, and a lost-or-damaged replacement charge for any mat that disappears. Contracts commonly run 36-60 months with automatic renewal and price escalators of 3%-5% a year. Those fees can lift the effective per-swap price by 25%-50% for a small account with only two or three mats.

blocks.title: Read the rental agreement before the per-swap price
blocks.text: Auto-renewal windows of 60-90 days, annual escalators, minimum weekly invoice amounts, and replacement charges for 'lost' mats are where rental programs get expensive. Ask for a written cap on surcharges and the right to change swap frequency seasonally without penalty.
Unit pricing for purchased mats maintained in-house

With owned mats, the cost has three parts: the purchase, the routine vacuuming, and periodic deep cleaning. Commercial-grade rubber-backed scraper and wiper mats commonly last two to four years in office entries, depending on traffic and whether they are rotated. Routine care is a nightly or per-visit vacuum pass, which takes a trained cleaner 1-3 minutes per mat. At ISSA-style production of roughly 3,500 sq ft per hour, that time is already inside a $0.07-$0.15 per sq ft per visit base rate for most offices, so it rarely appears as a separate line.

items: Routine vacuuming: 1-3 minutes per mat per visit, included in base janitorial pricing when entries are named in the scope.
Standalone mat care, if billed hourly: $35-$65 per hour standard labor, subject to a $90-$135 per visit minimum.
Hot-water extraction of mats: $0.30-$0.60 per sq ft of mat, or $8-$20 per 3 x 5 ft mat, typically monthly or quarterly.
Pressure washing rubber scraper mats outdoors: often bundled with exterior entry care at $35-$65 per hour.
Mat replacement reserve: budget the purchase price divided by expected life in months as a monthly sinking fund.

blocks.text: Side-by-side monthly cost for a typical entry

Take a single office entrance with one 4 x 6 ft wiper mat inside the vestibule and one 3 x 10 ft runner leading to reception. On a weekly rental cycle at midpoint pricing, that is ($6 + $10.50) x 4.33 = $71.45, plus a $15 stop charge per swap ($64.95) and a 5% surcharge, totaling about $143 per month. With purchased mats, nightly vacuuming is absorbed in the base rate, quarterly extraction of 54 sq ft of mat at $0.45 per sq ft amortizes to about $8 per month, and a replacement reserve for two commercial mats over a 36-month life typically lands in the $10-$20 per month range. Owned matting therefore costs roughly $20-$30 per month for that entry.

blocks.caption: Monthly cost comparison for one office entry (4 x 6 ft mat plus 3 x 10 ft runner)

blocks.text: Rental still wins in some situations. Snow-belt buildings that need double the matting from November to March, medical offices that want laundered mats for infection-control optics, and multi-tenant lobbies where no single janitorial vendor owns the entry can all justify the premium. Rental also shifts the burden of drying saturated mats, which can be a real problem in a small vestibule without a mop sink.
Minimum charges and how they distort small accounts

Both models have a floor. Route companies often set a minimum weekly invoice of $25-$40 regardless of mat count. Janitorial vendors apply per-visit minimums of $90-$135 if you ask for a standalone mat cleaning visit outside the regular schedule. For a 1,500 sq ft suite with two mats, those minimums can double the effective unit price, which is why small tenants almost always save by owning mats and adding them to the existing cleaning scope.

blocks.text: For crews maintaining owned mats, light gear keeps the work fast: a non-electric 9.5-inch commercial sweeper with dual debris bins handles daytime grit on mats and adjacent hard floors without cords, color-coded 16 x 16 in microfiber cloths (blue for general, red reserved for restrooms) wipe mat borders and door glass, and a 36-inch rubber-tipped litter grabber clears cigarette butts and debris from exterior scraper mats before vacuuming.

faqs.q: Is entrance mat vacuuming included in standard janitorial pricing?
faqs.a: Usually yes, if entry mats are named in the scope of work. Vacuuming mats takes 1-3 minutes per mat per visit and fits within base production rates. If your scope only says 'vacuum carpeted areas,' add explicit language covering entrance and walk-off mats so they are not skipped.

faqs.q: How do I calculate the monthly cost of a weekly mat exchange?
faqs.a: Multiply the per-swap price by the number of mats and by 4.33 weeks per month, then add the stop charge times 4.33 and any percentage surcharge. For two mats at $6 and $10.50 with a $15 stop charge and 5% surcharge, that is about $143 per month.

faqs.q: What hidden fees should I look for in a mat rental agreement?
faqs.a: Look for per-stop delivery charges, fuel or environmental surcharges, minimum invoice amounts, lost or damaged mat replacement fees, annual price escalators, and auto-renewal clauses with 60-90 day cancellation windows. These often matter more than the headline per-swap price.

faqs.q: How often should owned entrance mats be deep cleaned?
faqs.a: Most offices extract owned mats monthly in winter or wet seasons and quarterly the rest of the year, at roughly $0.30-$0.60 per sq ft of mat. Heavily used lobby mats may need monthly extraction year-round. Daily or per-visit vacuuming is still required between deep cleanings.

faqs.q: Do entrance mats have safety or compliance requirements?
faqs.a: OSHA walking-working surface rules require employers to keep floors free of slip and trip hazards, so mats must lie flat with no curled edges, and beveled edges help meet ADA accessibility expectations. Saturated mats should be swapped or dried promptly, and any cleaning chemicals used on mats need Safety Data Sheets under OSHA HazCom.
